about.label: about
about.title: Backend first, end to end when it counts
body: I'm a Computer Engineer from the Instituto Tecnológico de Costa Rica (TEC). Most of my work happens on the backend: designing REST APIs, modelling data, and moving legacy systems onto modern platforms without breaking what already works.

At Softland I migrated an ERP module from .NET Framework to Blazor on .NET 8. At Fundación Plan21 I built the APIs behind agricultural planning tools, including carbon footprint and evapotranspiration calculations.
I'm comfortable on the frontend too, with React and Vue, when a feature needs to go from the database to the screen.

softland-alerts.title: Moving an ERP module from desktop to the web
softland-alerts.summary: Migrated the Alerts module of the Softland ERP from .NET Framework to Blazor on .NET 8 and moved report storage into the database.
softland-alerts.context: Softland builds an ERP used by enterprise clients. Its Alerts module still ran on legacy .NET Framework with a desktop-only interface, and its REPX reports were stored as files that had to be shipped with every deployment.
softland-alerts.problem: The module had to reach users on any platform through the browser, without breaking how existing clients already used alerts, and report changes needed to stop depending on file deployments.
decisions: Blazor on ASP.NET Core / .NET 8 kept the whole module in C#, so the existing domain logic and the team's skills carried over to the web.
DevExpress 24.2 components provided the grids and reporting the ERP already relied on, keeping the new UI familiar to existing users.
REPX report definitions moved from files into the database, so a report can be added or updated as data instead of as part of a release.
results: The Alerts module runs as a cross-platform web application that replaces the desktop-only interface.
Report deployment effort dropped by an estimated 30%.

plan21-agro-api.title: APIs for data-driven farm planning
plan21-agro-api.summary: Backend endpoints for an agricultural platform: land-use planning, planting-time estimation, and carbon footprint and evapotranspiration calculations.
plan21-agro-api.context: Fundación Plan21 runs an agricultural management platform that helps farms plan how they use their land and when to plant.
plan21-agro-api.problem: Irrigation and planting decisions needed numbers behind them: how much water a crop loses to evapotranspiration and what its carbon footprint is, computed consistently for many farms.
decisions: Calculations were exposed as API functions instead of living in each client, so every feature of the platform gets the same results.
Farm and crop data lives in a relational database, which keeps the relationships between farms, land use and crops explicit and queryable.
Endpoints follow REST conventions, which keeps the platform's consumers simple and the API easy to extend with new calculations.
results: Land-use planning and planting-time estimation available for multiple farms.
Carbon footprint and evapotranspiration figures supporting irrigation and planting decisions.
